name: Learning from tiny amounts of data
gist: Training models that work well even when given very few examples, so they can adapt to new tasks quickly without massive datasets.
explain: Most multimodal models are trained on enormous datasets — millions or billions of image-text pairs scraped from the internet, or massive video corpora. But in the real world, labeled data is often scarce. You might have a hundred examples of chest X-rays labeled with diagnoses, but you need a model that works reliably. You might have a specific type of satellite imagery and only fifty examples, but you need to detect changes. In these situations, training a huge model from scratch is impossible — you do not have enough data. Instead, you take a model trained on large public data and adapt it to your specific task with only a few examples. This is called few-shot learning or low-data learning, and it works if the model can transfer knowledge from what it learned before.

The difficulty is that learning is usually noisy when you have tiny amounts of data. With a hundred examples, random noise in the labels, variations in the examples, and quirks of the small dataset can dominate. A model can easily memorize the few examples you give it without actually learning a generalizable pattern — this is called overfitting. How do you get a model to learn a reliable, general pattern from just a handful of examples? One path is through transfer learning: the model already learned to understand images and text from massive pretraining, so the hope is that this knowledge transfers to the new task even with few examples. Another path is through meta-learning, sometimes called learning to learn — the model is trained on many different small-data tasks during pretraining, so it learns strategies for learning quickly. A third path is through careful regularization — techniques that prevent the model from overfitting to the small dataset.

Research in this area focuses on making models that generalize from limited examples. Some approaches use prompting or in-context learning, where you show the model a few examples of the task and it learns to do it, all without updating the model's weights. This works surprisingly well with large enough base models. Others use parameter-efficient fine-tuning, techniques like adapters that add a small number of new parameters while keeping the main model frozen, so you do not overfit as easily. Some work builds models that can learn new categories of objects or new tasks with just a handful of examples by using techniques like prototypical networks, where the model learns to recognize new classes by comparing them to a learned prototype. Other work focuses on multimodal prompt learning, where both images and text are used as prompts to guide the model's behavior. The common goal is to build models that have enough learned knowledge to transfer to new contexts but remain flexible enough to adapt quickly to new domains with minimal data.

papers.title: Automatic Stage Lighting Control: Is it a Rule-Driven Process or Generative Task?
papers.contribution: Skip-BART outperforms conventional rule-based methods across all evaluation metrics and shows only limited gap compared to real lighting engineers.

papers.title: Bridging Radiology and Pathology Foundation Models via Concept-Based Multimodal Co-Adaptation
papers.contribution: Outperforms unimodal and fusion baselines (AUC 0.903 on TCGA-GBMLGG) while requiring only 0.15% additional parameters, enabling parameter-efficient multi-modal medical analysis.

papers.title: Meta-Adaptive Prompt Distillation for Few-Shot Visual Question Answering
papers.contribution: Achieves 21.2% improvement over ICL on VL-ICL Bench and 7.7% further enhancement compared to parameter-efficient finetuning methods for rapid task adaptation.

papers.title: One Patch Doesn’t Fit All: Adaptive Patching for Native-Resolution Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Delivers consistent improvements in native resolution performance with up to 2x throughput boost and 4x reduction in prefilling time.

papers.title: TAMMs: Change Understanding and Forecasting in Satellite Image Time Series with Temporal-Aware Multimodal Models
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms specialist baselines on both temporal change description and future image forecasting tasks with improved consistency.

papers.title: API: Adaptive Prototype Imputation for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI while establishing a robust, lightweight prototype-centric paradigm avoiding generative overhead.

papers.title: AQuA: Toward Strategic Response Generation for Ambiguous Visual Questions
papers.contribution: VLMs trained on AQuA achieve strategic response generation while outperforming baselines, demonstrating recognition of ambiguity and context-appropriate management.

papers.title: AlignedNorm: Prompting Vision–Language Models via Coupled Prompt Field
papers.contribution: Without complex designs, matches leading decoupled approaches on 15 datasets across 4 settings, offering new perspective and practical solution to local-optima dilemma in prompt learning.

papers.title: Criterion-Conditional In-Context Learning: Evaluating Criterion-Shift Adaptation in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Most MLLMs exhibit rigid boundary bias; simple multi-criterion training significantly improves Criterion Sensitivity, enabling 7B-scale models to surpass proprietary models.

papers.title: Language-Instructed Vision Embeddings for Controllable and Generalizable Perception
papers.contribution: LIVE reduces visual hallucinations by 34 points on MMVP, outperforms larger vision-language models on visual QA, and generalizes to unseen instructions and tasks.

papers.title: Referring Multiple Regions with Large Multimodal Models via Contextual Latent Steering
papers.contribution: LMMs with CSteer outperform dedicated referring LMMs in most cases, achieving state-of-the-art without fine-tuning or architectural modifications.

papers.title: SPR: A Structured Prompt Refinement Network for Modality Missing
papers.contribution: Uses only 0.8% trainable parameters; surpasses state-of-the-art by 3.8% F1-Macro on MM-IMDB at 90% modality missing rate.

papers.title: SpecPL: Disentangling Spectral Granularity for Prompt Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves 81.51% harmonic-mean accuracy as a universal plug-and-play booster for text-oriented baselines on 11 benchmarks.

papers.title: TASTE: Text-Aligned Speech Tokenization and Embedding for Spoken Language Modeling
papers.contribution: TASTE preserves paralinguistic information while reducing token sequence length and outperforms other pre-trained spoken language models on speech continuation and likelihood-based next-speech selection.

papers.title: Test-Time Optimization of 3D Point Cloud LLM via Manifold-Aware In-Context Guidance and Refinement
papers.contribution: PGLLM consistently improves accuracy and robustness over baselines with minimal additional computation cost on 3D datasets and out-of-distribution detection tasks.

papers.title: Text2Arch: A Dataset for Generating Scientific Architecture Diagrams from Natural Language Descriptions
papers.contribution: Introduces Text2Arch dataset with scientific architecture images, textual descriptions, and DOT code; fine-tuned models significantly outperform DiagramAgent and match GPT-4o performance.

papers.title: V-LynX: Token Interface Alignment for Video+X LLMs
papers.contribution: Achieves SOTA efficiency across audio-visual QA, 3D reasoning, high-frame-rate, and multi-view video understanding without paired supervision.
